home.faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
home.faq.a1: autoace-cli is the open-source bridge between an MCP AI client and the Kuaiyou Master App. It reads the current phone screen, validates skills, and sends them to the phone after you confirm.
home.faq.q2: Which AI tools do the docs cover?
home.faq.a2: The docs currently cover Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and generic MCP client configuration. Other MCP-compatible clients may work, but should be verified against their specific version.
home.faq.q3: Is root access required to run automation tasks?
home.faq.a3: No root is required. Kuaiyou Master uses Android Accessibility Services to execute actions; you still grant the required permissions and confirm before importing or running a skill.
home.faq.q4: Must AI stay connected while a skill runs?
home.faq.a4: No. AI helps inspect the screen and create the skill. After delivery and confirmation, Kuaiyou Master runs it on the phone. Reconnect only when you need changes.
home.faq.a5: autoace-cli, the Agent Skill, docs, examples, and skill JSON are open source. The Kuaiyou Master Android App and on-device execution engine are closed-source runtime components.

docs.intro.title: autoace docs
docs.intro.p1: Use autoace-cli (MCP) with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and similar tools to create skills in natural language, validate them, and push them to Kuaiyou Master for local execution. Optionally install the Agent Skill named autoace.
docs.intro.note: The Kuaiyou Master Android App is closed source and required for on-device execution. See Open-source boundaries at the end of this page.
docs.names.title: Names
docs.names.cli: MCP server / command-line tool (npm package / command). Required to connect AI and your phone.
docs.names.agent: Agent Skill (SKILL.md). Workflow instructions for Claude Code / Codex / Cursor. Optional but recommended.
docs.names.skill: Automation JSON that runs on the phone inside Kuaiyou Master — not a file you install into Claude/Codex.
docs.app.title: Get the Kuaiyou Master Android App
docs.app.p: Kuaiyou Master is the required phone runtime. It reads the screen and runs a skill locally after you confirm. Use the official product page to choose an app-store channel for your device.
docs.app.note: Follow the App setup to grant only the required permissions, then enable MCP Service under Settings → Advanced. Do not install unknown APKs from unofficial sources.
docs.install.title: Install autoace-cli
docs.install.p: autoace-cli is the MCP server and command-line tool of this toolkit (same npm package name). Once wired into your AI client, it can see the screen, validate skills, and push them.
docs.install.req.2: Access to the npm registry (or a working mirror)
docs.install.npx.desc: No global install. Uses the published package. Ideal as the MCP command in AI clients:
docs.install.global.desc: After install you can run autoace-cli directly (also usable as the MCP command):
docs.install.verify.desc: Check the version published on npm:
docs.install.tip: This binary is an MCP stdio server. Running it alone in a terminal waits on stdin. Normal use is letting your AI client launch it with KUAIYOU_DEVICE_IP / KUAIYOU_MCP_PAIRING_CODE.
docs.agent.title: Install Agent Skill: autoace
docs.agent.p: The Agent Skill autoace teaches the AI the MCP write → validate → push flow, plus HTTP fallback. It does not install phone-side skill JSON into the client.
docs.agent.claude.invoke: Use the personal path above, or share via .claude/skills/autoace/ in a repo. Invoke with /autoace.
docs.agent.codex.invoke: Or place under .agents/skills/autoace/ in a project. Invoke with $autoace or /skills. If missing, enable skills in Codex config and restart.
docs.agent.cursor.desc: Copy agent-skills/autoace into your project or personal Agent Skills directory, then start a new Agent session.
docs.quick.title: Configure MCP clients
docs.quick.p: After autoace-cli is available, enable MCP Service on the phone and put the connection info into your AI client. Prefer naming the MCP server autoace.
docs.quick.prereq.2: Kuaiyou Master installed on an Android phone
docs.quick.prereq.3: Enable MCP Service under Settings → Advanced, then tap the row to copy connection info (IP:port + pairing code).
docs.quick.prereq.4: The phone is on the same LAN as the computer, or connected via USB.

docs.write.title: Write your first skill
docs.write.lead: Drive it with natural language: the AI uses autoace-cli MCP to see the screen, write a skill, validate it, and push it. You usually should not hand-write JSON.
docs.write.flow.1: Confirm the client is connected to autoace MCP and MCP Service is on; optionally run /autoace.
docs.write.flow.2: Paste one of the prompts below (or adapt it to your goal).
docs.write.flow.3: The agent should call get_ui_tree / capture_screenshot first to understand the screen.
docs.write.flow.4: Then it should write a skill, run validate_kuaiyou_skill, and push_reactive_skill to the phone.
docs.write.flow.5: Confirm import/run on the phone. If it misses, keep chatting so the agent revises and pushes again.
docs.write.prompt: Prompts you can paste to the agent
docs.write.prompt.desc: Send the following to an AI client that already has autoace MCP configured:
docs.write.prompt.sample: Use autoace MCP: first capture_screenshot and get_ui_tree to inspect my phone screen, then write a skill that taps the Confirm button whenever it appears, up to 3 times with about 2s between taps. Validate with validate_kuaiyou_skill, then push_reactive_skill. Do not use removed readText / setClipboard — use storeValue for read/write.
docs.write.prompt.alt1: Look at the current screen, make a skill that taps Daily check-in, and push it to my phone.
docs.write.prompt.alt2: That miss-clicked — adjust the target from the latest screenshot and push another version.
docs.write.example: Example shape the agent may produce (reference)
docs.write.example.desc: This is only to illustrate skill JSON structure. Day-to-day, prefer agent generation + validation. More samples live under
docs.write.example.end: . Repo examples/skills are reference JSON, not the Agent Skill.
docs.write.tip: The phone asks for confirmation before import/run. Actions must be locally executable (tap, swipe, delay, storeValue, …).
